profiles.summary: No new reth or ruint release. A public endpoint now serves geth v1.17.10 built with go1.27.3, the second geth toolchain on the generated dispatch loop, and every battery, targeted, script and stack program run on it matched with the backend pinned before and after each call. Every released ruint from 1.18.0 to 1.21.1 still holds the two wrapping_from faults the changelog lists as unreleased fixes, and no interpreter on the list calls the faulty conversion.

deltas.delta: reth main still reports version 2.11.0 and now pins evm2 7c9f3b6d (cycle 17: 0a8a935c). Of the 35 evm2 interpreter, dispatch, stack, memory, gas and bytecode analysis files read in cycle 17, only bytecode/mod.rs differs, and only by a new unit test of the block access list code change conversion.

ruint's main changelog lists under Unreleased a wrong wrapping_from result and ValueNegative payload for negative primitive integers narrower than the Uint (#701) and for negative BigInts (#704). The TryFrom macro for i8 to i128 and isize is byte identical in the 1.18.0, 1.19.0, 1.20.0, 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 crates: a negative value is cast to the unsigned type of the same width and zero extended, so U256::wrapping_from(-1i64) gives 2^64 - 1 instead of 2^256 - 1. main replaces this with wrapping_from(unsigned_abs).wrapping_neg(). support/num_bigint.rs line 58 returns the unnegated magnitude in 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 and the negated one on main. Both faults are in every released version.

geth master (1.17.11-unstable) pins go1.27.4, the first Go release outside the range of Go issue 81863, drops the verkle (EIP-4762) table path and its code chunk charge from the interpreter, and applies EIP-8037 state gas refills after the charge of an opcode succeeds. interpreter_gen.go, instructions.go, stack.go, memory.go and analysis_legacy.go are byte identical to v1.17.10.

profiles.summary: Glamsterdam still has no Hoodi or mainnet date. reth's parallel executor for blocks with an access list, which Glamsterdam turns on, clears transient storage after every transaction a worker runs, commits worker results in transaction order, and rejects the block unless the access list rebuilt from that commit hashes to the header's.

deltas.delta: reth executes a block that carries a decoded access list through payload_processor/bal: each worker builds one executor, installs the received access list, sets the access index of each transaction and calls execute_transaction_without_commit, which in evm2 detaches the transaction overlay and calls clear_transaction_state, emptying transient storage (evm2 evm/tx.rs lines 240-249, evm/state/mod.rs lines 563-579). A failed worker rebuilds its EVM and state. The canonical executor commits the detached results in block order with the access list builder enabled (bal/execute.rs lines 157-196), and ethereum consensus validation compares the rebuilt hash with the header (validation.rs lines 113-131).

The Glamsterdam meta EIP lists only Sepolia (2026-10-06) with an activation. The Hegota meta EIP schedules EIP-7805 (FOCIL) and EIP-8141 (frame transaction) and has no date; cycle 8 already read EIP-8141 frames against the lock and the deltas.

profiles.summary: ETH stays the only gas asset. The only new item is geth master's handling of EIP-8037 state gas refills, which changes gas accounting after Glamsterdam and nothing a call returns before it.

deltas.delta: geth master adds dynamicCost.StateGasRefill and returns it to the contract's state gas after the opcode's charge succeeds (core/vm/interpreter.go, chargeDynamicGas). This is Amsterdam gas accounting for SSTORE that restores a slot, unreleased.

findings.title: A mainnet pool whose hook address has no code and sets the before remove liquidity flag holds a full range position that its owner cannot remove
findings.difference: No chain difference. An address without code answers any call with success and empty return data on Ethereum, and the pool's hook address 0xe16af6e33266e572bbcadb288bf3893942cd8220 has no code, nonce 0 and balance 0 at block 26,494,693.
findings.mechanism: Pool 0x462175db... (ETH and token 0x0b5702a3..., symbol tCURV, fee 100, tick spacing 1) was initialized at block 25,072,940 in transaction 0x1559b4e1..., which also minted PositionManager token 265,123 over the full range with liquidity 150,557,992,383,766,460,021. The hook address carries bit 9, the before remove liquidity flag. modifyLiquidity with a negative delta calls Hooks.beforeModifyLiquidity, which calls callHook on the hook. The call succeeds with no return data, so result.length is below 32 and callHook reverts with InvalidHookResponse. A read-only eth_call of PositionManager.modifyLiquidities from the token owner 0x7f715188103a3ed506e9dd95f918148b93875b22 with a full decrease returned revert data 0x1e048e1d, the InvalidHookResponse selector. The same call for token 292,697 in pool 0xf6aaf9bd..., whose empty hook sets only the after swap flag, passed the decrease and stopped at CurrencyNotSettled, as a decrease with no take should. The noSelfCall modifier skips the call only when the hook address itself is the caller, and this address has no code and has never sent a transaction. Code can appear there only through whoever can deploy to it or holds a key for it (EIP-7702), which is the F-013 case.
findings.impact: About 0.0054 ETH and 4,199,619 tCURV of one position stay in the PoolManager with no path out unless code appears at the hook address. The position was opened in the pool's creating transaction, so its owner chose the hook.
findings.preconditions: A pool whose hook address has no code and whose address bits include the before or after remove liquidity flag. Any pool creator can choose such an address, and liquidity providers who join it are bound by it.
findings.mitigations: Interfaces and routers should refuse to add liquidity to a pool whose hook has no code while any hook flag is set. Pool creators should use the zero hook for hookless pools.

sources.supports: eth_call of extsload(bytes32[]) on the PoolManager: pool 0x462175db... at tick 204,733 with active liquidity 150,557,992,383,766,460,021 and initialized ticks -887,272 and 887,272 only (cycles/021/ethereum-reference.work/l821.json); eth_getLogs ModifyLiquidity from block 25,072,940 to head finds the single mint (l821logs.json); eth_call of modifyLiquidities from the owner reverts with 0x1e048e1d (l821sim.json); eth_getCode of the hook returns 0x.

cleared.check: Lead L-940 by reading: do revm-interpreter 35.0.0, 37.0.3, 41.0.0, 42.0.0 and 43.0.2 or evm2 7c9f3b6d call ruint wrapping_from, saturating_from or TryFrom of a signed primitive or BigInt on an instruction path?
cleared.result: None does. A search of the instruction, stack, gas and dispatch sources for wrapping_from, saturating_from, checked_from, from(- and conversions from i8 to i128 finds only U256::from of usize, u64, bool and positive literals. Signed division, remainder, comparison and sign extension in both interpreters work on limbs: evm2 negates with (value xor mask) - mask over four u64 limbs (i256.rs lines 26-61) and revm uses two_compl on U256. revm-interpreter i256.rs, arithmetic.rs and bitwise.rs are identical from 37.0.3 to 43.0.2. So the #701 and #704 faults present in every ruint release cannot change SIGNEXTEND, SDIV, SMOD, SAR or SLT results used at src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:20-38, src/libraries/TickMath.sol:61-63, src/libraries/LiquidityMath.sol:12 and src/types/BalanceDelta.sol:24-39.

cleared.check: New vectors for L-940: 151 operands built from negative i8, i16, i24, i32, i64 and i128 values in both their correct 256 bit image and the zero extended image the ruint fault would produce, through SDIV, SMOD, SLT, SGT, SAR, SIGNEXTEND, ADD, SUB, MUL and the BalanceDelta and Slot0 unpacking sequence, 69,460 vectors.
cleared.result: No mismatch. geth v1.17.10 go1.27.3, geth v1.17.9 go1.27.2, geth v1.17.5 go1.25.12 and geth v1.16.7 go1.25.14 ran all 69,460 vectors, and reth v2.11.0 (ruint 1.21.1) ran 67,060, the rest refused with HTTP 403. cleared.check: geth master (1.17.11-unstable) interpreter files against v1.17.10.
cleared.result: interpreter_gen.go, instructions.go, stack.go, memory.go and analysis_legacy.go are byte identical. interpreter.go and jump_table.go remove the verkle table and its code chunk charge, which mainnet never enabled, and apply EIP-8037 state gas refills after the charge, which changes only Amsterdam gas. build/checksums.txt pins go1.27.4, outside the range of Go issue 81863.

cleared.check: Lead L-820: reth's parallel executor for blocks with an access list. Does each transaction start with empty transient storage, and is the rebuilt access list checked against the header?
cleared.result: Yes to both. A worker executes each transaction with execute_transaction_without_commit, which detaches the overlay through take_pending_state and calls clear_transaction_state, which clears transient_storage together with the journal, logs and warm sets (evm2 evm/tx.rs lines 240-249, evm/state/mod.rs lines 563-579); a nested transaction gets committed_copy with an empty transient map (lines 135-150). The canonical executor commits worker results in block order and builds the access list from that commit (reth bal/execute.rs lines 157-196), and validation.rs lines 113-131 reject the block when the rebuilt hash differs from the header's. So the unlock flag, deltas and synced currency in src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-26 and src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 cannot cross from one transaction to the next on this path. A builder that ships a false access list only gets its block rejected, which is an operator matter.

cleared.check: Upcoming forks within six months, assumed shipped the day after: Glamsterdam's 20 scheduled EIPs and Hegota's two scheduled ones.
cleared.result: The scheduled list matches what cycles 14 and 17 cleared: new opcodes that the PoolManager bytecode never decodes (EIP-7843, EIP-8024), gas repricing (EIP-2780, 7778, 7976, 7981, 8037, 8038), ETH credited outside a call or a burn removed (EIP-7732, 8246, 8282), logs (EIP-7708), code size (EIP-7954), the existing CREATE2 factory (EIP-7997) and access lists (EIP-7928, read above for reth and in cycle 17 for geth). Native settlement credits msg.value only (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364), so ETH arriving without a call books to no one. Hegota schedules FOCIL, which changes inclusion only, and EIP-8141 frames, which cycle 8 read. Neither fork has a mainnet date.

cleared.check: Lead L-885: who created the Ethereum copy of the PoolManager at 0x8366a39c..., what it holds, and whether it gives anyone a path to the Robinhood Chain or Arc PoolManager funds at the same address.
cleared.result: EOA 0x629f191e... created it at block 25,466,547 through the deterministic CREATE2 factory 0x4e59b448... with a zero salt, so the address follows from the factory, the salt and the creation code with the owner 0x9701fb0a... as constructor argument. Anyone can repeat that creation on a chain that has the factory and get the same address only with the same owner, so a replica on another chain is owned by 0x9701fb0a... and not by its deployer. It holds 0 ETH, 10 initialized pools, no ModifyLiquidity, Swap or ERC-6909 Transfer event since creation, and nonce 1. Nothing on Ethereum moves value at the other chains' addresses. Whether a bridge or interface treats the three as one principal is an integration question outside src/.

cleared.check: Lead L-821: liquidity outside the current tick in the 21 pools on hooks that are empty or EIP-7702 delegated, with pool ids recomputed from each pool key.
cleared.result: No pool has liquidity outside its current tick: every initialized tick range of the four pools that hold liquidity contains the current tick. Cycle 17's census stored the initializing transaction hash in its poolId field (pool 0x462175db... is listed as 0x1559b4e1..., the hash of its creation transaction), so its reading of zero in-range liquidity for all 21 was taken at slots no pool uses. Read at the right slots, four pools hold liquidity: 0x08834f72... (delegated hook, about 0.0059 ETH and 1.03 USDC), 0x992c0ab6... (delegated hook with after remove and after remove returns delta, about 0.0038 ETH), 0x462175db... (empty hook with before remove, frozen, see finding) and 0xf6aaf9bd... (empty hook with only after swap, about 1,000 units of 0x0e90b620... and 2.33 USDT, removable). F-013's measured Ethereum exposure is therefore a few dollars, not nil.

cleared.check: Lead L-822: a public mainnet endpoint for erigon or nethermind that serves eth_call with state override.
cleared.result: None found among 75 endpoints probed with web3_clientVersion. The only erigon backend (tatum, erigon 3.8.2 go1.27.4) answers eth_call only on paid plans, and no endpoint named nethermind. Gateways that hide the backend (drpc, cloudflare, mevblocker, tenderly, thirdweb) cannot be pinned.

leads.question: Can the remaining cycle 17 census rows (pools on hooks with code) have been read with the same transaction hash in place of the pool id, and do any other clearances or findings rest on hooks7702.json or the cycle 5 Initialize scan that produced it?
leads.why: This cycle found that the census poolId field holds creation transaction hashes, which voided its liquidity reading for the 21 pools; any other use of that field is void in the same way.

leads.question: When ruint publishes the #701 and #704 fixes, or a release after 1.21.1, does it change any path besides wrapping_from and the BigInt conversion, and do the battery, targeted set and narrowneg.py vectors still match on a reth build that pins it?
leads.why: Every released version carries both conversion faults, the fix release is the next one reth and Tempo will pin, and 1.21.0 showed that a release can bring a new arithmetic fault.

leadResults.answer: No public endpoint serves eth_call with state override from erigon or nethermind on mainnet. 75 endpoints were probed on 2026-11-25; the only erigon one (tatum, erigon 3.8.2) limits eth_call to paid plans, and none reports nethermind.

https://public-eth.nownodes.io serves Geth/v1.17.10-stable-1df30b18/linux-amd64/go1.27.3, a different toolchain from go1.27.2 and the merged DUP and SWAP loop of v1.17.10. battery.py (99,985), targeted.py (85,544), pushdup.py (229 of 232, 3 rate limited) and pmdiff.py (248 of 250 compared) gave the specified results with no mismatch, and every bracket read before and after each eth_call that answered named that build. No public endpoint serves a go1.27.4 geth yet; blockrazor's go1.25.12 build is v1.17.5, which predates the generated loop, and it also matched.

reth's BAL worker clears transient storage after every transaction it runs (evm2 evm/tx.rs lines 240-249, evm/state/mod.rs lines 563-579), the canonical executor commits worker results in block order and rebuilds the access list, and ethereum consensus validation rejects a block whose rebuilt hash differs from the header (validation.rs lines 113-131), as geth v1.17.9 does.

Not run. Building evm2-jit needs LLVM 23, which is not installed here, and installing software is ruled out. The JIT stays off unless an operator enables it (F-129), and its IR builders were transcribed in cycle 15.

No pool among the 21 holds liquidity outside its current tick. Cycle 17 read the wrong slots: its poolId field held transaction hashes. Recomputed from the pool keys, four pools hold in-range liquidity, and one of them, 0x462175db..., has an empty hook with the before remove liquidity flag, so the owner's full removal reverts with InvalidHookResponse in a read-only eth_call. That position (about 0.0054 ETH and 4.2 million tCURV) is frozen. Recorded under F-004 with actor pool-creator.

ruint 1.18.0, 1.19.0, 1.20.0, 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 all contain both faults: the signed primitive TryFrom is byte identical across them and zero extends negative values, and num_bigint.rs returns the unnegated magnitude in 1.20.1 and 1.21.1. The mul_mod fix #681 is in 1.21.1 only. revm-interpreter 35.0.0 to 43.0.2 and evm2 7c9f3b6d never convert a signed primitive or BigInt to U256 on an instruction path, and their signed opcodes work on limbs, so no opcode result the PoolManager uses depends on the fault. 69,460 new vectors aimed at narrow negative operands matched on the endpoints listed in cleared. mega-evm wraps the stock revm instructions (OPCODES.md) and was not read separately.

Created at Ethereum block 25,466,547 by EOA 0x629f191e... through the CREATE2 factory 0x4e59b448... with a zero salt and owner 0x9701fb0a... as constructor argument. It holds 0 ETH, 10 initialized pools and no liquidity or claims. A replica elsewhere at that address must carry the same owner. Bridge and interface treatment is an integration matter outside src/ and was not studied.
